doc: twoody/security-code/v1 — the « code de sécurité » of a computer, shown to people (twoody-server login, the server's admin page, GET /account/link on its console, Twoody Desktop, the app) to compare two screens before trusting a computer. Reference: src/vault/contracts.ts securityCode.

Derivation: digest = SHA-256( UTF-8('twoody/security-code/v1') || the computer's X25519 tunnel public key as its 32 raw bytes ). Take the first 100 bits of the digest, most significant bit first, as 20 groups of 5 bits; each is a character of Crockford's base32 alphabet '0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ' (value 0 = '0', 31 = 'Z'; no I, L, O, U). Written in 4 groups of 5 joined by '-': 'XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX' (23 characters).

Which key: the tunnel key the computer's binding names (computer-binding-v1 / desktop-binding-v1 tunnel_public_key; GET /api/v1/peer/vault/identity tunnel_public_key). The 8-hex `fp` (Bonjour, account pairing key) stays a discovery hint only.
Reading one typed by a person (optional): upper-case it, drop '-' and spaces, read O as 0 and I or L as 1 before comparing.
label: twoody/security-code/v1
